sources.entry: impacket - A collection of Python classes for working with network protocols, widely used for Windows and Active Directory testing.

summary.one_liner: Impacket is a Python library of classes for constructing, parsing and speaking network protocols (SMB, MSRPC, Kerberos/NTLM auth, and more), shipped with example tools built on it.
summary.what_it_does: Impacket provides low-level programmatic access to network packets, letting users build packets from scratch, parse raw data, and work with protocol hierarchies through an object-oriented API. It includes high-level implementations of NMB and SMB1, SMB2 and SMB3, plus MSRPC version 5 over TCP, SMB/TCP, SMB/NetBIOS and HTTP transports. It supports plain, NTLM and Kerberos authentication using passwords, hashes, tickets or keys. The README lists partial or full implementations of many MSRPC interfaces (such as SAMR, LSAD, RRP, SCMR, TSCH, DCOM and WMI), and portions of the TDS (MSSQL) and LDAP protocols. The library also ships example tools that show what can be done with it.
use_cases: Build or parse network packets in Python
Interact with SMB shares and file systems
Make MSRPC calls to Windows services
Test Kerberos or NTLM authentication with hashes or tickets
Explore Active Directory protocols such as LDAP and SAMR
Prototype or research network protocol implementations
how_to_run: python3 -m pipx install .   (for the development version, run from the unpacked source directory)
notable: Object-oriented packet construction and parsing across Ethernet, IP, TCP, UDP, ICMP, ARP and more
SMB1, SMB2 and SMB3 plus MSRPC implementations over several transports
Kerberos, NTLM and plain authentication using passwords, hashes, tickets or keys
Originally created by SecureAuth, now maintained by Fortra's Core Security
SMBv1 and NetBIOS support based on Pysmb by Michael Teo
caveats: README states it is for research and educational purposes and not meant for production environments or commercial products
Some protocol implementations are only partial (e.g. TDS/MSSQL and LDAP)
